# Background and purpose {#intro}

The [Northeast Regional Ocean
Council](https://www.northeastoceancouncil.org/) (NROC) and
[Mid-Atlantic Regional Council on the
Ocean](https://midatlanticocean.org/) (MARCO) coordinate with providers
and users of seafloor data to understand potential needs and
applications.

NROC and MARCO convene working groups composed of decision makers and
seafloor data experts in each region to continually advance the
understanding of existing seafloor data, data gaps, data management
workflows, and seafloor data products needed for ocean planning and
management.

Federal agencies that collect seafloor data (or fund seafloor data
collection) usually make those data available via federal data
platforms, including:

- The [International Hydrographic Organization Data Centre for Digital
  Bathymetry](https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/iho-data-centre-digital-bathymetry)
  hosted at NOAA NCEI

- U.S. Geological Survey Coastal and Marine Hazards and Resources
  Program [Imagery Data System](https://cmgds.marine.usgs.gov/idsviewer)
  \| [Samples Repository Collections
  Inventory](https://cmgds.marine.usgs.gov/wh/samples/#home)

- Seafloor data collection funded by the National Science Foundation
  (NSF) is stored in the [Marine Geoscience Data
  System](https://www.marine-geo.org/index.php)

However, state agencies, other research entities, and partners in the
private sector that collect seafloor data (or fund and/or require the
collection of seafloor data) expressed a need for a platform to store,
access, and transmit seafloor data for use in regional data products and
future research. The recommendation for such a platform was also
articulated in the [RWSC Science
Plan](https://rwscollab.github.io/science-plan/seafloor.html#data-management).
NROC and MARCO developed a Seafloor Data Repository where data providers
from multiple sectors could make data findable and accessible to meet
these needs.

The purpose of this Seafloor Data Repository (SDR) is to catalog and
make available seafloor datasets in U.S. Atlantic waters collected by a
variety of entities and purposes that can eventually be used to develop
regional-scale seafloor habitat data products (e.g., bathymetry maps,
benthic habitat maps, surficial seafloor geology maps) for wider use and
dissemination via the Mid-Atlantic Ocean Data Portal and Northeast Ocean
Data Portal, and other mapping platforms.

Anyone may contribute data (or just metadata) to the SDR to provide for
discoverability and accessibility of seafloor data in our regions of
interest.

*Please see the information in the*
[Support](https://seafloor.dataone.org/support) *tab for general
guidance on publishing data.*

# Requiring submission to the Seafloor Data Repository {#requiring}

State and federal agencies who are funding research or otherwise
requiring the collection of seafloor data are encouraged to require
submission of seafloor data and data products to the Seafloor Data
Repository. Use and/or modify the language below to include a
requirement in a research grant/contract agreement or permit
condition/stipulation.

> Contractor/permittee must submit data and data products (defined
> below) resulting from the activities described herein to the Seafloor
> Data Repository (<https://seafloor.dataone.org>) within 1 (one) year
> of collection.
>
> Contractor/permittee must follow the instructions and specifications
> in “Submitting Data to the Seafloor Data Repository (SDR)” available
> at:
> [https://rwscollab.github.io/sdr](https://rwscollab.github.io/sdr/)
>
> Data should be submitted according to the specifications listed in
> “Submitting Data…” including by uploading the specific file types at
> the requested resolution. The resolutions requested are intended to
> obscure confidential business information, proprietary information, or
> sensitive seafloor features (e.g., cultural or national security).
> Contractor/permittee must provide agency/funder with a reasonable
> explanation for submission of data at different resolutions or any
> omission of data and data products due to concern about
> confidentiality or sensitivity.

# Types of data accepted {#types}

The SDR stores data collected by any entity (federal, state, private
company, research institution). Through funding from the Massachusetts
Clean Energy Center, Rhode Island Department of Environmental
Management, and U.S. Bureau of Ocean Energy Management, the following
variables, formats, and resolutions were collaboratively identified by
an NROC expert working group ([INSPIRE and NROC
2023](https://github.com/RWSCollab/sdr/blob/main/files/RegionalHabitatMapping_REPORT_Final_w_Appendices.pdf)).
These recommended variables, formats, and resolutions were selected and
designed specifically to obscure potentially sensitive or confidential
seafloor features (whether related to cultural resources or national
security concerns).

|  |  |  |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| **Seafloor variable(s)** | **Type/format** | **Desired resolution** |
| Multibeam bathymetry | Raster/tiff | 8m\* |
| Multibeam backscatter | Raster/tiff | 8m\* |
| Boulder fields and/or picks (identification of boulder locations) | Vector-points/polygons Esri shapefile | N/A |
| Seabed interpretation – CMECS Substrate Group, Subgroup | Vector-points/polygons/Esri shapefile | N/A |
| Seabed interpretation – Shell substrate | Vector-points/polygons/Esri shapefile | N/A |
| Seabed interpretation – Bedforms | Vector-polygons/Esri shapefile | N/A |
| Seabed interpretation – CMECS Biotic Subclass | Vector-points/Esri shapefile | N/A |

^\*\*Before uploading, bathymetry and backscatter mosaics should be down-sampled to the recommended resolution. A [Down-sampling Protocol](https://github.com/RWSCollab/sdr/blob/main/files/Appendix_C_Downsampling_Protocol.pdf) is available to assist data providers.\*^

Files containing confidential and/or sensitive information should not be
uploaded to the Seafloor Data Repository. In these instances, metadata
can be submitted to the Seafloor Data Repository, and the dataset entry
can be labeled with the appropriate Data Sensitivity tag (see [Steps for
data submission](#steps)).

# Steps for data submission {#steps}

1.  Email emily.shumchenia\@rwsc.org to let us know you’re planning to
    submit a data package to the SDR.

2.  You must be signed in to DataONE’s platform to submit data. This can
    be done by entering your [ORCID](https://orcid.org/). If you don’t
    have an ORCID, you can obtain one for free at
    [https://orcid.org](https://orcid.org/).

3.  From the home page at <https://seafloor.dataone.org/>, select
    “Submit Data” from the header menu.

4.  The Submit Data page contains two sections. The top section is a
    tool to upload files. The bottom section is a data submission form.

5.  Check that your metadata meets or exceeds the [RWSC Essential
    Metadata](https://rwscollab.github.io/repositories-data-catalog/essential-metadata-guide.html)
    guidelines. You will use this information to fill out the data
    submission form. The Seafloor Data Repository will automatically
    generate an EML (Ecological Metadata Language) metadata file using
    the information you submit. The metadata file will be available as
    part of your data record. *Note: EML is the metadata standard used
    by several RWSC/NROC/MARCO recommended repositories including OBIS
    and GBIF.*

6.  Fill out all pages/subsections of the [data submission
    form](https://seafloor.dataone.org/submit) completely and
    accurately. Pay special attention to listing your research funder(s)
    with their identifiers (e.g. [ROR](https://ror.org/)) (use the
    *organization* and *userId* fields).

7.  Based on the Data Sensitivity level that you assign to the data,
    upload data files using the tool at the top of the Submit Data page.
    If you select “Some or all data is sensitive with significant risk”,
    **do not upload files** but continue to complete the metadata
    submission.

8.  Hit the “Save dataset” button at the bottom of the page to send your
    data submission to the SDR curators for review and publication.

# What to expect after submission {#after}

1.  Your data remains private and will not appear in the SDR until SDR
    curators have reviewed it. SDR curators are:

- Emily Shumchenia, RWSC Director, NROC Science & Portal Director
  ([[emily.shumchenia\@rwsc.org]{.underline}](mailto:emily.shumchenia@rwsc.org))

- Nikelene Mclean, RWSC Coordinator, Habitat & Ecosystem Subcommittee
  Coordinator
  ([[mclean.nikelene\@gmail.com]{.underline}](mailto:mclean.nikelene@gmail.com))

2.  During the review process, SDR curators may reach out to you with
    questions about the data or to discuss any sensitivities

3.  Upon publication, curators will provide you with a DOI linked to the
    page specific to your dataset in the SDR. We encourage you to use
    the DOI to add the dataset to publication records, CVs, and
    websites, and to cite the data wherever they are mentioned to
    increase data discovery and reuse.

4.  Once the data is published, it will appear in the SDR on the “Search
    Data” page. If you uploaded data, anyone can download it and the
    associated metadata. DataONE will track how many times a dataset has
    been downloaded, cited, and viewed. These metrics will be shown on
    your dataset’s SDR page.
